title: `corr`: shared state; NaN for one pair or zero variance
verdict: dp_xy / sqrt(dp_xx · dp_yy); NaN where the reference is NULL; no clamp
description: `PearsonState` returns `dp_xy / sqrt(dp_xx * dp_yy)` if `dp_xx * dp_yy > 0`, else NaN: one pair or a zero variance is NaN. Not clamped to [-1, 1]. `dp_xx * dp_yy` can overflow or underflow before the square root.
No pairs: null in the streaming reducer; the in-memory path (`polars-ops` `cov.rs`) returns NaN.

Integers become doubles (`as f64`) and decimals are cast to `Float64` in memory, so the degenerate cases are those of doubles: one pair or a constant side is NaN for `Int64` and `Decimal` too. Above 2⁵³ distinct integers can round to one double: `corr` of 2⁶², 2⁶² + 1, 2⁶² + 2 with 1, 2, 3 is NaN.

The streaming reduction accepts primitive numerics only: `corr` of a `Decimal` column raises `InvalidOperationError` on the default lazy engine and succeeds in memory. No pairs is null when streaming and NaN in memory (above).
The docs are silent on one pair, a constant side and no pairs, the types `corr` takes and the engines: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins no pairs or a `Decimal` input; they may change between versions.
Probed: `pl.corr(x, 2x)` is 1.0 for {4, 7, 13, 16} shifted by up to 1e12 on the streaming engine, ungrouped and grouped; a constant side is NaN.
reference: `AggFn.corr` (`corrOf`): NULL for fewer than two pairs, or for a side whose values are all equal; else the co-deviation sum by the square root of the product of the two squared-deviation sums. It is not clamped to [-1, 1]. Engines may differ in the last bits (#54) until #85 bounds the error.
Where the reference is NULL (one pair, a constant side), Polars gives NaN.
